blocks: ## T01 - Hayakawa's house and inner court redrawn to the research (FR-001)
## T02 - the two kept houses recorded as deviations (FR-002)
## T03 - the procedure for a new magistracy (FR-003)
## T04 - the record's figure and the close (FR-001)

decisions.summary: Hayakawa's house about 65 tsubo (kitchen, bath, corridor counted), top of 0091's range as a GUESS for the RICH knob; room zones GUESS
decisions.why: FR-001: the house within 49-67 tsubo; the GM: 'the third magistracy should be corrected'. Placing it at the top of the range for a rich posting is a choice inside the range, labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: Hayakawa's inner court laid out again around the smaller house: alley, privies, roji, kitchen ell, bath, inner entrance, storehouses, woodshed, karo's house, vegetable garden, shrine moved
decisions.why: FR-001: 'whatever on the Hayakawa sheet does not correspond to the research is brought to it'; the request: 'whatever other changes need to be made should be made'. Re-laying the court around a house a third its size is the consequence of the correction, not a new scope; the karo's house is kept at its measured 0118 size.

decisions.summary: Hayakawa's north wall moved 30 ft south (envelope a knob), guests' annex with it, coverage to about 30.6%
decisions.why: Departs from the standing 'envelope NOT shrunk' rule for this sheet. The question put to the GM told him a redraw drops coverage to 27-28%, under 0116's band; he chose the redraw and added 'whatever other changes need to be made should be made in order to make the whole thing correspond to our research'. 0116's band is research, and FR-001/SC-001 require the sheet inside it. The alternatives are priced: a recorded deviation is forbidden by SC-001, inflating buildings past research sizes defeats the request's own purpose, west/east walls are physically blocked by the gate range and outer court. The rule's purpose (a smaller wall must not hide slack) is not gutted: the program is research-sized and cannot be grown honestly. Owed, not ruled: the notes call the envelope 'the audited Joge<->Takayama size, a range'; the plan does not state the shrunk envelope still sits inside that range, and T01 should measure and say so, or else record what it leaves.

decisions.summary: The standing rule amended for magistracy sheets: when the research resizes the program, the envelope follows the coverage band (docs/buildings.md checklist, coverage-check messages, the test pinning the text)
decisions.why: As applied to magistracy sheets this is authorized in the GM's words: 'we should correct our general procedures when creating new magistracy diagrams in order to correspond to our research'; FR-003 requires a new sheet kept within 0116's band, 'how, the plan's'. Without it the procedure would order a research-sized house inside Ochiba's 141-tsubo envelope and land under the band.

decisions.summary: The same amendment's reach as worded: 'when the research resizes A SHEET'S program, the envelope follows it', in the shared coverage-check messages (pack_audit/shared.py, registry.py) and the general checklist - every sheet type, not magistracies
decisions.why: Nothing in request.md speaks to any sheet but the three magistracies and 'new magistracy diagrams'. 'Whatever other changes NEED to be made' covers what this correction needs; neither Hayakawa's redraw nor the magistracy procedure needs a standing rule relaxed for temples, farmhouses or any other compound. Generalizing it is completing the GM's thought. Fix: word the amended checklist line and both messages (and the pinned test) for a magistracy sheet whose house the research sizes, not 'a sheet's program'; or put the general form to the GM.

decisions.summary: T01 Approach item 2: 'The outer court is not touched.'
decisions.why: FR-001 and SC-001 sweep the whole Hayakawa sheet ('whatever on the Hayakawa sheet does not correspond to the research is brought to it'; 'every element of the sheet the research speaks to corresponds to it'). The plan measured coverage and the karo's house but records no check of the outer court against the research, so excluding it rests on an unmeasured premise. As a layout constraint (the outer court is not moved to make room, which D3's pricing of (c) and (d) relies on) it is within; as worded it cuts FR-001's scope. Fix: 'the outer court is not moved to make room; FR-001's correspondence sweep over it is still owed through building-review'.

decisions.summary: The house keeps its recorded forms (echelon of two blocks, reception at the east end, roji, kitchen ell, veranda faces)
decisions.why: Corrects the size the GM asked corrected and keeps the forms nothing in the request or research is said to contradict; building-review remains the occasion for the sheet.

decisions.summary: docs/buildings.md :17 and :23, Ochiba notes :65 and Ubame notes :109 say DEVIATION with the GM's reason (about 141 and 152 tsubo); Hayakawa's figure becomes ~65 tsubo
decisions.why: FR-002 verbatim: 'two of them should stay the same as recorded deviations, because ... significantly wealthier magistrates than normal'. No ink changes on either sheet (T02 constraint) matches 'stay the same'.

decisions.summary: docs/building-programs.md residence bullet and a docs/buildings.md checklist line state 49-67 tsubo, a larger house only as a recorded deviation, envelope follows the band; docs/usage.md keeps Ochiba as template for conventions and drawing but says its house is a deviation not to be copied
decisions.why: FR-003 and the GM: 'correct our general procedures when creating new magistracy diagrams'. FR-003 removes Ochiba only as the model for the house's size; keeping it as the template for other conventions is inside that. The envelope clause here is magistracy-scoped (D3b), not the general reach of D3c.

decisions.summary: 0116's drawing page sentence gives each compound's measured coverage on its date, Ochiba re-measured too
decisions.why: The record states Hayakawa's coverage (35%), which the redraw changes; making the record match the measured sheet is part of 'make the whole thing correspond to our research'. Re-measuring Ochiba's stated figure is the standing measure-not-remember rule on a figure already in the record, not new scope.
